title: The Born Representation Theorem and the Unistochastic Theorem
abstract: This paper presents self-contained, constructive proofs of two new theorems about stochastic matrices, with direct relevance to quantum theory. The first theorem, herein called the Born Representation Theorem, shows that each entry of any stochastic matrix can be expressed as the trace of a pairwise product of matrices, where the first factor in the pairwise product belongs to a positive-operator-valued measure (POVM) and the second factor belongs to a projection-valued measure (PVM). As its name suggests, this theorem entails that the entries of any stochastic matrix can be expressed in terms of a generalized version of the quantum-theoretic Born rule. It follows as a corollary that if the POVM in this first theorem is a PVM, then the stochastic matrix is unistochastic, meaning that its entries are each the modulus square of the corresponding entry of a unitary matrix of the same size. The second theorem proved in this paper, called the Unistochastic Theorem, then shows that by dilating the underlying vector space by a bounded number of additional dimensions if necessary, each entry of any stochastic matrix can be expressed in terms of the trace of a pairwise product for which both factors belong to PVMs, and can thus be derived via marginalization from a larger unistochastic matrix. This second theorem therefore establishes a kind of primacy of unistochastic matrices over stochastic matrices, and hints at a close connection with unitary time evolution in quantum theory. The paper concludes with a brief discussion of potential applications to discrete-time deterministic processes and Markov chains.
summary: This paper develops two theorems connecting stochastic matrices to quantum probability theory. It shows that any entry in a stochastic matrix can be written as a trace involving generalized quantum measurement operators (POVMs and PVMs). Crucially, it establishes that these processes are fundamentally linked to unistochastic matrices, suggesting that unitary evolution dictates the structure of all discrete-time probabilistic systems.
main_problem: To establish deep mathematical connections between stochastic matrices, which model classical probabilistic processes (Markov chains), and the probability rules derived from quantum mechanics.
main_result: The paper proves that any entry of a stochastic matrix can be expressed as a trace involving POVMs and PVMs (Born Representation Theorem), and further shows that these entries are fundamentally constrained by unistochastic matrices, suggesting a primacy of unitary evolution structures.
method: Constructive proofs utilizing properties of Positive-Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) and Projection-Valued Measures (PVMs) within the framework of trace formulas.
model_or_system: The model centers on stochastic matrices $\Gamma$ describing conditional probabilities $p(i|j)$ in discrete-time Markov chains. These are related to quantum systems via PVMs $\{P_j\}$ and POVMs $\{E_i\}$, which generalize the standard Born rule.
key_observables: The entries of the stochastic matrix $\Gamma_{ij}$, representing conditional probabilities, and their representation as traces involving quantum measures.
important_parameters: The dimensions $M 	imes N$ of the stochastic matrix; the structure of the underlying POVMs and PVMs.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that classical probabilistic processes can be mapped onto structures derived from quantum measurements (POVM/PVM formalism).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Born Representation Theorem, showing $\Gamma_{ij} = 	ext{tr}(E_i P_j)$. It then proves a corollary relating this to unistochastic matrices. Finally, it presents the Unistochastic Theorem, demonstrating that any stochastic matrix can be derived from marginalizing a larger unistochastic structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical bridge between classical Markovian dynamics and quantum unitary evolution by showing how general probabilistic processes are constrained by structures related to unitaries (unistochastic matrices).
